A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoMAS research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training trajectories and component, agent-number and agent-diversity ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds SRLM comparisons, repeated evaluations, 7B-model results, resource measurements and reward-quality analyses.

M1.justification: The solution, evaluation and scoring procedure, agent selection, complementary rewards and REINFORCE++ optimization remain unchanged. Equations 1–11 are retained; revised descriptions and testing a 7B backbone do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MATH, KodCode and WebInstruct-verified training mixture and the same seven evaluation benchmarks across four inference setups. The additional model experiments and science failure examples do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds self-rewarding language models (SRLM) as an evaluated baseline in all four Table 1 inference setups. Untrained agents, MAPoRL and TTRL remain. SRLM was previously cited but lacked reported comparison results.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, resource profiling with stated fixed interaction rounds, and reward precision/recall measured against verifier-provided ground truth. Existing 3B settings, benchmark sampling limits and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged. The newly stated use of REINFORCE++ for baseline RL training does not establish a change to earlier runs.

E4.justification: Appendices D, G and J substantially extend the analyses with resource scaling, reward accuracy against ground truth over training, and concrete failure trajectories without evaluation or scoring. The original component, agent-number and diversity ablations remain, with their detailed tables moved from Appendix C to Appendix H.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. v2 Appendix E and Table 4 report means and standard deviations over five evaluation seeds for all five methods and seven benchmarks under Vanilla inference. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting, although repeated training runs and formal significance tests are not reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds SRLM scores, five-seed summaries, 7B-model results, resource measurements and reward-quality trajectories. Existing Table 1 rows and the original ablation-table values remain unchanged. Figure 4 swaps assignments between the two ablations: the Vanilla 'w/o Evaluation' bar changes from -0.78 to -0.03 points, creating disagreement with retained Table 7, while the reward-curve assignments now match the prose.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and Equations 1–11 are retained. No theorem, proof or formal derivation is added. The new cost-scaling discussion presents empirical observations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: autonomous learning from interaction rewards, decentralized co-evolution without external supervision, competitive benchmark performance and scalability with agent number and diversity. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a resource tradeoff: scaling requires substantially more computation and memory despite nearly constant reported wall-clock time. It also interprets the new evaluations as statistically significant and attributes performance gains to improving reward accuracy. These extend existing interpretations without replacing the central explanation.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports token counts, memory consumption and training time, and explicitly documents REINFORCE++ for baseline RL training. Existing hyperparameters are retained. The availability statement changes from 'dataset and code' to 'code'; the PDFs do not establish that dataset access was actually withdrawn.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the general reinforcement-learning overview and substantially refocuses positioning around static, dynamic and learnable multi-agent systems, distinguishing collective reasoning from individual-agent evolution. Numerous associated RLHF, preference-optimization, reward-model and social-simulation references are removed. This exceeds bibliographic or organizational editing.

P1.justification: Related work is rewritten, main-results discussion is shortened, and existing appendix sections are reordered. The example trajectory receives wording and formatting edits, while affiliations, conference headers and acknowledgments change. The introduction, methodological narrative and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The results presentation expands substantially through four new appendix tables and SRLM rows in Table 1. Figures 3–5 are reformatted, including Figure 4's changed result assignments; Figure 2 receives revised labels and a rewritten caption. Retained appendix tables and boxed examples are relocated and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added SRLM comparison, five-seed summaries and 7B replication strengthen evidence that was missing from v1. Resource and reward analyses also improve assessability. The benefit is limited by evaluation-only uncertainty estimates, significance claims without a reported formal test, and reward-mechanism conclusions that exceed the observed trends. Figure 4 also introduces a bar-to-table inconsistency while correcting its reward-curve assignments. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
